findings.title: Silence menu item can be shown but the silence drawer never opens for ruler-less rules
findings.body: In the ruler-less list flow, RuleActionsButtons receives only promRule. AlertRuleMenu can therefore show the 'Silence notifications' item based on Grafana Prometheus abilities, and clicking it sets showSilenceDrawer to true. However, the drawer is only rendered when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true, and rule is undefined in this flow. The result is a visible, clickable Silence action that does nothing. The drawer should be rendered from the Prometheus rule data or the menu item should be hidden/disabled when no ruler rule is available.

findings.title: Grafana list items are rendered without a React key
findings.body: FilterViewResults maps over rules and computes a key for each item, but in the 'grafana' case it returns GrafanaRuleListItem without key={key}. The datasource and unknown branches do pass a key. Missing React keys can cause reconciliation warnings and incorrect reuse of component state across list items when results are appended or updated.

findings.title: skipToken does not produce neutral Grafana abilities
findings.body: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities converts skipToken to undefined and still evaluates useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities. With an undefined rule, some abilities are not neutral: for example Duplicate can become supported and allowed based on global Grafana create permissions. This can make actions appear in contexts where there is no Grafana rule, such as non-Grafana Prometheus rules or missing promRule data. skipToken should return [false, false] for all requested actions.

findings.title: Federated rules are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: useAllRulerRuleAbilities hard-codes isFederated = false, and the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities wrapper no longer checks the original rule group with isFederatedRuleGroup. Previously, federated rules were considered immutable and update/delete/duplicate actions were hidden. After this change, federated rules may be shown as editable or deletable in the UI, which is a permission/contract regression unless federation support is intentionally being removed.

findings.title: Delete is not rendered for Grafana Prometheus-only rules even when allowed
findings.body: canDelete is computed from either ruler abilities or Grafana Prometheus abilities, but the Delete menu item is only rendered when canDelete && rulerRule. In the ruler-less alert list view rulerRule is undefined, so users with delete permission will never see Delete for Grafana rules. If deletion is intended to remain available after removing ruler fetches, this condition needs to support Prometheus-only rules.

findings.title: Grafana rule key contains an extra closing brace
findings.body: getGrafanaRuleKey returns a string ending with an extra '}' after rule.uid. The key is currently not used in the Grafana branch because the key prop is missing, but the malformed key will be confusing if reused later.

findings.title: Clipboard copy promise has no rejection handler
findings.body: navigator.clipboard?.writeText(text).then(...) does not handle promise rejection. If clipboard access is denied or fails, the app can produce an unhandled promise rejection and the user receives no feedback. A catch handler should be added.

findings.title: Inline action arrays defeat memoization in ability hooks
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu passes new array literals to useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities on every render. Those hooks memoize their result based on the actions array reference, so the mapped abilities are recomputed on every render for every row. Extracting the action list to a stable constant would avoid unnecessary work in large rule lists.
